findings.title: Google Calendar credential key is saved as Zod SafeParseReturnType `{ success: true, data: ... }` instead of the token object
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), whereas previously `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned the parsed token object directly. On lines 97-100, `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` is written straight to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. After the first token refresh, the stored `credential.key` in the database becomes `{ success: true, data: { ... } }`, so the next time `GoogleCalendarService` is instantiated `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) will fail with a Zod validation error and break Google Calendar integration for that user.

findings.title: `prisma` is not imported in Salesforce `CalendarService.ts` and `refreshOAuthTokens` is never called
findings.body: `prisma.credential.update` is called on line 96, but `prisma` is not imported anywhere in `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`. This causes a TypeScript compilation error and a `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` at runtime whenever Salesforce is used. Additionally, the token refresh `fetch` on line 75 was not wrapped in `refreshOAuthTokens`, and lines 106-107 pass the stale `credentialKey.access_token` to `new jsforce.Connection(...)` instead of the newly refreshed `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`.

findings.title: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses `[z.string().toString()]` which defines literal `"[object Object]"` keys and strips expiry fields
findings.body: In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` evaluate `toString()` on Zod schema instances, producing the literal property name `"[object Object]"` (and overwriting the first with the second). Because `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` strips every field except `access_token` (including `expires_in` / `expiry_date`) and does not require any numeric expiry field. Callers such as Zoom (`newTokens.expires_in * 1000`), Google (`token.expiry_date`), and Office365 then compute `NaN` or `undefined` for the token expiration.

findings.title: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response`, breaking callers that expect an Axios/googleapis response with `.data`
findings.body: When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` calls `fetch(...)` and returns a standard `Response` object (where the JSON payload is accessed via `await response.json()`). However, several callers pass callbacks that return objects with a `.data` property and immediately read `res.data`: `GoogleCalendarService` (`const token = res?.data` on line 94), `BiginCalendarService` (`tokenInfo.data` on line 96), `ZohoCrmCalendarService` (`zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` on line 217), and `HubspotCalendarService` (which expects a parsed `HubspotToken` object directly on line 192). When syncing is enabled, `res.data` is `undefined` and token refresh throws a `TypeError` in all of those integrations.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin passes `credentialId` instead of `credential.userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens`
findings.body: `refreshAccessToken` receives `credentialId` (`credential.id`) and passes it as the third argument (`userId`) to `refreshOAuthTokens` on line 93. `refreshOAuthTokens` sends this value as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint, so the sync endpoint will be queried with the credential's primary key ID rather than the Cal.com user's ID.

findings.title: Requests to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are sent without any authentication header
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` sends a `POST` request with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and no secret or signature header (such as `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). Any party that can reach `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` can request fresh OAuth access tokens for arbitrary `calcomUserId` values without authentication.
